quotes.text: This is the fundamental shift. Protection needs to move from the infrastructure layer to the data layer itself. Instead of just guarding the building, you need to guard the files inside it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the core idea behind data-centric protection.

quotes.text: Here's the thing about labels, they travel with the data, if a document is marked confidential and someone attaches it to an email, the label stays attached.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear explanation of why sensitivity labels are persistent.

quotes.text: Compliance is about proving your secure, not just being secure. You can have the best protections in the world. But if a regulator shows up and asks for evidence, you need more than good intentions.

quotes.text: If your data isn't properly classified, co-pilot might surface sensitive information to someone who shouldn't see it. Not because the system is broken. Because the data was never labeled,

quotes.text: Here's the single most powerful thing you can do right now. Run the data classification scan. Just run it. Knowing what you have changes everything
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

chapters.title: Why walls around data are not enough

takeaways: Microsoft Purview moves protection from the network to the data itself through governance, security and compliance.
Sensitivity labels travel with documents and drive DLP policies, which you should test in simulation mode before enforcing.
Copilot exposes unlabeled, overshared data, so start with a data classification scan and use Compliance Manager as your roadmap.
hook: Firewalls do nothing once a trusted user moves sensitive data. This episode explains Microsoft Purview in simple terms for IT, security and compliance teams, showing how governance, sensitivity labels, DLP and Compliance Manager work together, including for Copilot and AI.
